```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, error = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.height = 4.8, fig.width = 9, fig.align = "center")
options(knitr.kable.NA = "—")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table); library(ggplot2); library(knitr); library(kableExtra)
  library(scales); library(jsonlite)
})
if (!identical(params$render_token, "rendered-by-09_uncertainty_psa")) {
  stop("Render through psa_render_documents() in code/09_uncertainty_psa.R.")
}
dd <- params$data_dir
rd <- function(f) fread(file.path(dd, f), encoding = "UTF-8")
man <- fromJSON(file.path(dd, "run_manifest.json"))
reg <- rd("parameter_register.csv")
pdraws <- rd("parameter_draws.csv")
md <- rd("mortality_draws.csv")
sm <- rd("mortality_summary.csv")
tab_g <- rd("table_global_interventions.csv")
tab_r <- rd("table_who_region_all_interventions.csv")
val <- if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "validation_log.csv"))) rd("validation_log.csv") else NULL
tchk <- if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "transition_checks.csv"))) rd("transition_checks.csv") else NULL
n_mc <- man$n_mc_draws_successful
reportable <- isTRUE(man$reportable)
tier <- if (is.null(man$interval_tier)) (if (reportable) "preliminary" else "technical") else man$interval_tier
ui <- if (reportable) "95% UI" else "technical-check interval"
prelim <- if (tier == "preliminary") "preliminary " else ""
n_mc_f <- format(n_mc, big.mark = ",")
cmp <- if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "manuscript_comparison.csv"))) rd("manuscript_comparison.csv") else NULL
int_order <- c("HTN Control (No Diabetes)", "HTN Control (Diabetes)", "Improved Statin Uptake", "All Interventions")
int_cols <- c("HTN Control (No Diabetes)" = "#1f78b4", "HTN Control (Diabetes)" = "#a6cee3",
              "Improved Statin Uptake" = "#e31a1c", "All Interventions" = "#6a3d9a")
region_order <- c("Western Pacific", "South-East Asia", "Europe", "Americas", "Eastern Mediterranean", "Africa")
f2 <- function(x, d = 2, s = 1) formatC(round(x / s, d), format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
S <- function(geo, sid, m) sm[who_region == geo & scenario_id == sid & metric == m]
ui_txt <- function(x, d = 2, s = 1e6) sprintf("%s [%s–%s]", f2(x$point, d, s), f2(x$lower, d, s), f2(x$upper, d, s))
theme_psa <- function(base = 13) theme_minimal(base_size = base) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
g_all <- S("Global", "all_interventions", "deaths_averted")
g_pct <- S("Global", "all_interventions", "percent_averted")
g_base <- S("Global", "all_interventions", "baseline_deaths")
```

`r if (tier == "final") sprintf('<div style="background:#2f3e55;color:white;padding:12px 16px;font-weight:bold;border-radius:4px;">95%% uncertainty intervals from %s Monte Carlo draws of the BP and statin intervention-effect parameters. They do not represent total uncertainty: coverage, targets, adherence, epidemiology, calibration and secular trends are fixed.</div>', n_mc_f) else if (reportable) sprintf('<div style="background:#5b4a1f;color:white;padding:12px 16px;font-weight:bold;border-radius:4px;">PRELIMINARY ESTIMATES &mdash; 95%% uncertainty intervals from %d Monte Carlo draws. Tail precision is limited; the intervals are not converged estimates and reflect BP and statin intervention-effect parameter uncertainty only.</div>', n_mc) else sprintf('<div style="background:#b30000;color:white;padding:12px 16px;font-weight:bold;border-radius:4px;">TECHNICAL CHECK &mdash; %d draws. Software test of the PSA pipeline; the intervals are not reportable.</div>', n_mc)`

# Summary

Achieving all three modelled WHO targets together (Targets 1 + 2 + 3) is projected to avert
**`r ui_txt(g_all)` million** cardiovascular deaths between 2026 and 2050
(`r f2(g_pct$point, 1, 1)`% [`r f2(g_pct$lower, 1, 1)`–`r f2(g_pct$upper, 1, 1)`] of the
`r f2(g_base$point, 1, 1e6)` million deaths projected under business-as-usual). The point estimate
is the deterministic model result`r if (!is.null(cmp) && all(cmp$match)) " (identical to the manuscript's central estimate)" else ""`; the bracketed
range is a `r prelim``r ui` from `r n_mc_f` draws of the **BP and statin intervention-effect
parameters**. Every other input is held fixed, so the range is not total uncertainty.

```{r table-global}
  footnote(general = paste0(
    "Deaths averted = business-as-usual deaths minus deaths under the intervention, summed over countries, ",
    "the four modelled causes (ischaemic heart disease, ischaemic stroke, intracerebral haemorrhage, ",
    "hypertensive heart disease), both sexes, ages 20–95 and calendar years 2026–2050 within each draw. ",
    "Average per year = cumulative / 25. Point = deterministic model (draw 0); brackets = 2.5th–97.5th ",
```

# What was sampled

The analysis is a probabilistic sensitivity analysis of **intervention-effect parameters only**.
One parameter vector is drawn per iteration and shared by every country, age, sex, year and
scenario, so all scenarios within a draw are matched.

## BP effects (BPLTTC 2021, Appendix S6)

The 15 hazard ratios per 5-mmHg SBP reduction that the model's effect workbook traverses
(ischaemic heart disease, stroke and heart failure; baseline SBP 130–139, 140–149, 150–159,
160–169 and ≥170 mmHg) are drawn as log(HR) ~ Normal(log HR, SE²) with SE = (log U − log L)/3.92
from the reported 95% CIs. The workbook's `Sheet1` columns are rebuilt for each draw with the
workbook's own formulas (RR per 10 mmHg = HR5², cumulative products over traversed bins), feeding
both the no-diabetes and diabetes subgroup effects. Stroke HRs feed both ischaemic stroke and
intracerebral haemorrhage, as in the model. The BP case-fatality reduction constants
(0.24, 0.36, 0.76, 0.20 per unit of incremental control) stay fixed: no endpoint-matched
source with uncertainty is available (a documented gap, see the register).

```{r bp-table}
bp <- pdraws[family == "BP"]
bps <- bp[, .(Point = value[draw_id == 0L],
              `Draw 2.5%` = quantile(value[draw_id > 0L], 0.025, names = FALSE),
              `Draw 97.5%` = quantile(value[draw_id > 0L], 0.975, names = FALSE)), by = .(param_id, endpoint, stratum)]
src <- reg[family %like% "^BP efficacy" & status == "SAMPLED", .(param_id, ci = sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", ci_lower, ci_upper),
                                                                  sdlog = round(sdlog, 4))]
bps <- src[bps, on = "param_id"]
kable(bps[, .(Outcome = endpoint, `Baseline SBP` = stratum, `HR per 5 mmHg` = sprintf("%.3f", Point),
              `Source 95% CI` = ci, sdlog, `Sampled 2.5–97.5%` = sprintf("%.3f–%.3f", `Draw 2.5%`, `Draw 97.5%`))],
      caption = sprintf("Sampled BP parameters (draws 1–%d).", n_mc)) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 12, full_width = FALSE)
```

## Statin effects (CTT Collaboration)

The four relative risks hard-coded in the model's statin function are sampled as
log(RR) ~ Normal(log RR<sub>model</sub>, SE²), SE = (log U − log L) / (2 · z<sub>(1+c)/2</sub>),
with draw 0 exactly at the model values. Every RR-dependent statin quantity, including the
baseline-coverage denominator 1 − (1 − RR)·coverage<sub>0</sub>·adherence, is recomputed in each draw.
All four RRs are per 1.0 mmol/L LDL-cholesterol reduction; the model applies them unscaled as the
effect of statin use, and that convention is retained. Draws with RR > 1 are kept (no truncation).

```{r statin-table}
stt <- reg[family %like% "^Statin efficacy"]
kable(stt[, .(Parameter = sub(" in calculate_statins_impact\\(\\)", "", model_variable), `Model value` = model_point,
              Source = sub("\\.$", "", sub(" et al.*", " et al.", source)), Endpoint = source_endpoint,
              `Published RR (CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f), %d%% CI", source_point, ci_lower, ci_upper,
                                            round(100 * ci_level)),
              sdlog = round(sdlog, 4))],
      caption = "Statin parameters: verified sources, confidence levels and log-scale SDs.") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 12, full_width = TRUE)
```

Notes on the statin evidence (full text in `parameter_register.csv`):

* **IHD incidence (0.74).** Fulcher et al. (CTT, *Lancet* 2015;385:1397–405) report major coronary
  events (non-fatal MI or coronary death) RR 0.76 (95% CI 0.73–0.79) for all 27 trials. The model
  value 0.74 equals the men-only estimate in the same figure (RR 0.74, 99% CI 0.70–0.78) and also,
  numerically, the lower 99% limit of the CTT 2010 coronary-death RR quoted beside it in the model code.
  The distribution is therefore **centred on the retained model value with precision borrowed from
  the all-participant 95% CI**; the point estimate itself is not changed.
* **Ischaemic-stroke incidence (0.80).** Fulcher et al. 2015, webappendix stroke subtypes: first
  ischaemic stroke RR 0.80 (95% CI 0.75–0.86). Endpoint and point match.
* **IHD and ischaemic-stroke case fatality (0.80, 0.96).** Fulcher et al. 2015 do not report coronary or
  stroke death separately. The values match the CTT 2010 meta-analysis cited in the model code
  (*Lancet* 2010;376:1670–81): death from coronary heart disease RR 0.80 (**99%** CI 0.74–0.87) and
  death from stroke (any type) RR 0.96 (95% CI 0.84–1.09). These are unconditional mortality endpoints
  in trial populations. **Using them as multipliers on conditional case fatality among prevalent cases is
  a modelling assumption**: the trials did not estimate conditional case fatality, and part of the
  mortality reduction reflects fewer incident events, which the incidence RRs already capture. The
  stroke-death interval crosses 1, so some draws imply a small case-fatality increase.
* **Correlation.** No joint covariance is published: the four statin RRs are drawn independently of
  each other and of the BP parameters (working assumption).

```{r fig-statin, fig.height=3.6}
sd <- pdraws[family == "statin" & draw_id > 0L]
pt <- pdraws[family == "statin" & draw_id == 0L]
ggplot(sd, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "#e31a1c", alpha = 0.55, colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(data = pt, aes(xintercept = value), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Relative risk (per 1.0 mmol/L LDL-C)", y = "Draws",
       title = "Sampled statin relative risks", subtitle = "Solid line = model value (draw 0); dashed = RR 1") +
  theme_psa(11)
```

## What is fixed

Coverage targets and trajectories (150 million additional controlled hypertensives by 2030 split by
diabetes status; ≥50% statin coverage by 2030), statin adherence (`r man$run_args_06$adherence_ir` /
`r man$run_args_06$adherence_cf`), the GBD high-FPG attributable fraction and the 0.60
atherosclerotic share of ischaemic stroke, BP distributions and the GBD exposure–risk gradient,
diabetes shares, calibrated baseline rates, coherent secular mortality trends, population and COVID
excess mortality. The intervals are **BP and statin intervention-effect parameter uncertainty
intervals**, not total uncertainty.

## Tail precision

With `r n_mc` draws the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles rest on few observations in each tail. The
table gives distribution-free 95% confidence ranges for each interval endpoint (order statistics);
wider ranges mean less precise endpoints. A larger run (the draw count is configurable) narrows them.

```{r tail}
tp <- sm[metric == "deaths_averted" & !is_fixed]
tp[, Group := fifelse(geography_level == "global", intervention, paste0(who_region, " (All Interventions)"))]
kable(tp[, .(Group, `Point (M)` = f2(point, 2, 1e6), `UI (M)` = sprintf("%s–%s", f2(lower, 2, 1e6), f2(upper, 2, 1e6)),
             `Lower endpoint range (M)` = sprintf("%s–%s", f2(lower_os95_lo, 2, 1e6), f2(lower_os95_hi, 2, 1e6)),
             `Upper endpoint range (M)` = sprintf("%s–%s", f2(upper_os95_lo, 2, 1e6), f2(upper_os95_hi, 2, 1e6)),
             `MC mean (M)` = f2(mc_mean, 2, 1e6), Draws = n_draws)],
      caption = "Deaths averted, 2026–2050: interval endpoints and their order-statistic precision.") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 12, full_width = TRUE)
```

```{r fig-running, fig.height=3.8}
ga <- md[geography_level == "global" & scenario_id == "all_interventions" & draw_id > 0L][order(draw_id)]
if (nrow(ga) >= 10L) {
  ns <- seq(10L, nrow(ga), by = 5L); if (tail(ns, 1) != nrow(ga)) ns <- c(ns, nrow(ga))
  run <- rbindlist(lapply(ns, function(n) data.table(n = n,
    lower = quantile(ga$deaths_averted[seq_len(n)], 0.025, type = 7, names = FALSE),
    upper = quantile(ga$deaths_averted[seq_len(n)], 0.975, type = 7, names = FALSE))))
  ggplot(run, aes(x = n)) + geom_line(aes(y = lower / 1e6), colour = "#6a3d9a") +
    geom_line(aes(y = upper / 1e6), colour = "#6a3d9a") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = g_all$point / 1e6, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(x = "Number of draws", y = "Deaths averted (M)",
         title = "All Interventions: interval endpoints as draws accumulate",
         subtitle = "Dashed = deterministic point") + theme_psa(11)
}
```

# Methods

* **Model.** The current Aim 1 model (`r man$script06`, md5 `r man$script06_md5`) is used read-only:
  its saved inputs (calibrated rates with coherent secular trends from stage 031, UNWPP population,
  COVID excess mortality, BP and statin inputs, the 150M BP-control target table) are loaded exactly as
  the production pipeline loads them; no stage of the production pipeline is re-run or modified.
  Scenarios: `r paste(man$scenarios, collapse = ", ")`; `all_interventions` applies the two BP
  subgroup effects (as an additive population mixture, using the `bp_combined` targets) followed by the
  statin effects, with the model's own combination equations and its 0.99 caps on incidence and case
  fatality. `bp_combined` is simulated for consistency and validation only and is not reported.
* **Propagation.** For each draw, the BP subgroup incidence effects and all statin incidence and
  case-fatality multipliers are recomputed and passed through the model's sequential well–sick–dead
  transitions (2017–2050, ages 20–95, four causes). A batched implementation of the same equations is
  used for speed; it is checked against the model's own code draw by draw (validation below).
* **Estimands.** Within each draw: deaths = sum of cause-specific CVD deaths over locations, causes,
  sexes, ages and the 25 years 2026–2050; deaths averted = baseline − projected; per year = averted / 25;
  % averted = 100 × averted / baseline. Regions aggregate the same country set as the global total.
* **Intervals.** Point = deterministic model (draw 0, not part of the quantiles; it need not lie inside
  the interval). Interval = 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles (type 7) of draws 1–`r n_mc`, seed
  `r man$seed`. `r if (tier == "final") sprintf("With %s draws the endpoint precision is shown in the tail-precision table; draws 1-N are stable across run sizes, so a smaller run is a prefix of this one.", n_mc_f) else sprintf("These are **preliminary** intervals: %s draws give limited tail precision.", n_mc_f)`
* **Transition validity.** The model caps incidence and case fatality at 0.99 and floors negative
  states at zero; sampled RRs above 1 are allowed. The number of capped cells is monitored per draw
  (validation V11).

# Validation

```{r validation}
if (!is.null(val)) {
  val[, V := sub("^(V[0-9]+).*$", "\\1", check)]
  vt <- val[, .(Checks = .N, Passed = sum(pass %in% TRUE), Failed = sum(pass %in% FALSE),
                Informational = sum(is.na(pass)),
                `Max abs diff` = { x <- max_abs_diff[is.finite(max_abs_diff) & !is.na(pass)]; if (length(x)) signif(max(abs(x)), 3) else NA_real_ }),
            by = .(Check = sub(" \\(draw [0-9]+\\)$", "", sub(", draw [0-9]+$", "", check)))]
  kable(vt, caption = sprintf("Validation summary: %d hard checks, %s.", sum(!is.na(val$pass)),
                              if (isTRUE(man$validation_all_pass)) "all passed" else "SOME FAILED")) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 11, full_width = TRUE)
}
```

Key results: draw 0 reproduces the saved deterministic model output for every country, scenario and
state cell; the batched engine reproduces the model's own code (re-homed with each draw's parameters)
for the reference draws; BP-only perturbations change only the BP scenarios and All Interventions, and
statin-only perturbations change only Improved Statin Uptake and All Interventions;
`r v6 <- if (is.null(val)) NULL else val[grepl("^V6", check)]; if (!is.null(v6) && nrow(v6) && all(v6$pass %in% TRUE)) "draw-0 aggregates reproduce the deterministic report's global and regional tables." else "the comparison of draw-0 aggregates with the deterministic report was not run for this geography."` `r if (!is.null(tchk)) { x <- tchk[draw_id > 0L]; x0 <- tchk[draw_id == 0L]; sprintf("Across draws, the number of incidence/case-fatality cells at the 0.99 cap ranged %s–%s (draw 0: %s), so capping is not consequential.", min(x$n_ir_capped + x$n_cf_capped), max(x$n_ir_capped + x$n_cf_capped), paste(unique(x0$n_ir_capped + x0$n_cf_capped), collapse = "/")) } else ""`

```{r isolation, results='asis'}
iso <- if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "isolation_report.csv"))) rd("isolation_report.csv") else NULL
n_iso <- if (is.null(man$isolation_changes_outside_output_psa)) NA else man$isolation_changes_outside_output_psa
if (isTRUE(n_iso == 0)) {
  cat("**Path isolation:** no file outside `output_psa/` changed during the run.\n\n")
} else if (!is.na(n_iso)) {
  cat(sprintf("**Path isolation:** %d file(s) outside `output_psa/` changed during the run:\n\n", n_iso))
  print(kable(iso[status %in% c("ADDED", "MODIFIED", "REMOVED")], caption = "isolation_report.csv") |>
          kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "condensed", full_width = FALSE, font_size = 11))
  if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "isolation_diagnosis.md"))) {
    cat("\n\n", paste(readLines(file.path(dd, "isolation_diagnosis.md"), encoding = "UTF-8")[-1], collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")
  }
}
```

Files in `output_psa/`<code>`r man$run_id`</code>`/`: `parameter_register.csv`, `parameter_draws.csv`,
`mortality_draws.csv`, `mortality_summary.csv`, `table_global_interventions.csv`,
`table_who_region_all_interventions.csv`, `validation_log.csv`, `transition_checks.csv`,
`run_manifest.json`, `checkpoints/` (compact per-block totals for resumption) and `rendered/`.
